# Memory

## Scope and Ownership

Maintain reusable terminology and technical conventions for wireless communications writing here. Keep prose style and rhetorical preferences in `style_profile.md`. Apply glossary terms only when relevant to the manuscript.

## Technical Terminology

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Channel knowledge map (CKM) | A location-indexed representation of channel-related knowledge that supports environment-aware wireless communication and sensing. |
| Environment-aware communications | Wireless communication design that uses site-specific or environment-specific knowledge rather than relying only on instantaneous channel acquisition. |
| B2X CKM | A CKM indexed from a fixed-position base station to arbitrary receivers or users. |
| X2X CKM | A CKM indexed by both transmitter and receiver positions to characterize arbitrary transmitter-receiver channel relations. |

## Abbreviations and Notation

- At first use, give the full term followed by its abbreviation in parentheses, unless the abbreviation is universally standard for the target venue.
- Keep each term, abbreviation, and symbol consistent throughout the manuscript. Introduce technical objects and symbols where first needed.


## Safe Phrase Bank

- "we investigates..."
- "The key difficulty lies in..."
- "This observation motivates..."
- "To address this issue, we..."
- "Numerical results indicate that..."
- "These results support ..."

## Manuscript Conventions

- Keep LaTeX source minimal and avoid decorative formatting.
- Make captions understandable on their own and define figure-specific abbreviations or symbols as needed. The division of content between captions and prose is specified in `style_profile.md`.
- Check symbol and cross-reference consistency and cite figures in order of appearance.
